findings.title: Protocol authority and executable drift
closure_evidence: PF-001 at 0acaba7f25f228477908c2c4bc81a69609f4b682: all five artifacts the authority record classes as prototypes carry the gate, their normative owner and every recorded incompatibility and prohibited use in their own source, enforced by validate_artifact_quarantine.py.

PF-004 at f98a31502f6863e0c29dc97c0f3b233c919d1b32: every mutable aggregate declares revision_model, transaction_boundary and outbox, with the four combinations outbox_events.unique(aggregate_id, aggregate_revision) forbids rejected by validate_state_vocabularies.py.

PF-002 at 2d9935ee7cc5c950b68243a671395776f31e20b8: nothing read a CDDL rule name against a vector file in either direction, so the exact-byte vectors could have encoded a different message entirely and passed. The acceptance was unsatisfiable as written — zero of the 26 rule names appear in either file, because both hold hex. cddl_instance.py now decodes both payloads and header maps, requires each to satisfy its rule with the exact label set, and re-encodes to the committed bytes; the pinned, corpus-pinned and declared-unpinned rule sets must partition the grammar exactly. VIBEPROOF_V1_CANONICAL_PROFILE.md was a second document owning canonical encoding while describing the eleven-field shadow codec, which is this finding in one file.

PF-003 at 2d9935ee7cc5c950b68243a671395776f31e20b8: the evidence-ceiling check did not exist. run_evals.py admitted authority_class and evidence_ceiling to its allowlist with a comment saying they carry no execution semantics, and read neither; one suite of 27 carried them. All 27 now do, the vocabulary is declared once in artifact-authority-v1.json and read rather than copied, and a manifest binding no fixtures caps at none so absence lowers the ceiling instead of escaping the check. What remains for SR-005 is outside this finding: protocol/vibeproof-v1.cddl is unquarantined while four of its consumers are exploratory prototypes, and registering it needs a notice inside protocol/, which this phase may not write.

findings.title: OAuth, linked identity, recovery, and ranked identity
closure_evidence: PF-005 at cb04718c0e21ab365ea55ebe2e9c9a8763bff8f0: the OAuth provider registry exists and the mix-up control is evaluable. /auth/github/callback declared the RFC 9207 iss parameter and /auth/x/callback did not, while reason-codes-v1.json bound OAUTH_ISSUER_MISMATCH to both; the parameter deferred to a stored provider-capability record that did not exist, so ADR-015's control could not be evaluated at all. Sixteen mix-up vectors are derived from the registry rather than listed.

PF-006 at cb04718c0e21ab365ea55ebe2e9c9a8763bff8f0: every identity mutation reaches one transaction. linkIdentity took a bare authorization_code, so redirect, state, PKCE, provider revision and lifetime were optional in practice; oauth_transactions now binds all eighteen bindings the contract names, four as check constraints, and intended_action had no CHECK at all in the DDL while the API spelled it snake_case.

PF-007 at cb04718c0e21ab365ea55ebe2e9c9a8763bff8f0: unlinking a provider account was silently permanent product-wide: provider_subject was not null under a total unique (provider, provider_subject), so a retained unlinked row blocked that provider account from ever being linked to any account, and DATA_MAP.md's delete-on-unlink promise could only be honoured by deleting the row the constraint required. Both personal-data fields are now null exactly when the binding has ended.

PF-008 at cb04718c0e21ab365ea55ebe2e9c9a8763bff8f0: consolidation has a path. The account-consolidation machine declares consolidation-confirm with actor user and the API declared no consolidation operation at all, so a case left awaiting-confirmation only by expiring. D-564, that the older ranked identity survives, was recorded in no machine-readable place and is now checkable with a matched negative fixture.

findings.title: Device lineage, challenge, replay, checkpoint, and recovery
closure_evidence: PF-009 at 48b22762fcce6d84650f352867f717ae9df41920: device_sequences keys on lineage_id and no longer references a device row, continuity_state has one owner in device_lineages, and claim_challenges carries a lineage_id foreign key. A copied device store previously produced two internally continuous rows, making the fork invisible to the counter meant to catch it.

PF-010 at c7647fe7bb1f171588106de8c14d9f20cdb4be34: lineage scoping was enforced where the sequence counter is read and not where it is written. D-592 rekeyed device_sequences onto the lineage and stopped one table short: claims still carried unique (device_id, device_sequence) and unique (device_id, payload_hash), so two device rows in one lineage could each hold sequence 42 and the same payload. checkpoint_receipts was device-keyed while the head it advances was lineage-keyed, giving a restored store a private receipt chain. device_key_events could not record dual authorization at all — one nullable signature and no account column — so an ordinary rotation and a single-signature forgery were the same row. All three are repaired, with recovered forbidding the outgoing signature so a rotation cannot be admitted by claiming to be a recovery. AUTHENTICATION_AND_RECOVERY.md also ended the recovery order with a human appeal, contradicting D-561's accepted rule that exhaustion is permanent.

findings.title: Local daemon, shell, IPC, and platform supervision
closure_evidence: PF-011 at 355755b365f3b1ee0ac158255af21a103303ea1d: all eight local roles are declared once in packages/schemas/local-trust-domains-v1.json with an OS peer identity per platform, a session boundary, an explicit network scope and capability, data-class and prohibition lists. PLATFORM_KEY_AND_PRIVILEGE_MATRIX.md tabulated six and omitted the interactive shell and the privileged supervisor — the only role taking arbitrary operator input and the only one running elevated. The separation the privacy boundary rests on is enforced: exactly one role may read transcript-content and its network scope is none. The local channel protocol, shell/subsystem separation and local persistence remain open under PF-012, PF-013 and PF-014.

PF-012 at da930f9c961ef9d029b68e9bb1aee3561551af2c: local-control-v1.proto reaches every message body only through its own role's arm, so a collector encoding a deletion request is unrepresentable rather than rejected. Envelope previously carried one universal oneof holding all fifteen bodies with sender_role a field the sender filled in, while LOCAL_IPC_AND_DEVICE_IDENTITY.md stated that role confusion is rejected. Three local-channel reason codes now exist for what remains detectable; the protocol previously had no vocabulary with which to refuse anything. Shell/subsystem separation and local persistence remain open under PF-013 and PF-014.

PF-013 at da930f9c961ef9d029b68e9bb1aee3561551af2c: interactive-shell declares only the eight process and connection states. It previously carried fifteen, collapsing collection, sync, auth, permission, update and connectivity into one state variable, so a device with paused collection and an offline network had no representable shell state. Five projections now persist in local-store-v1.sql. Local persistence and migration remain open under PF-014.

PF-014 at da930f9c961ef9d029b68e9bb1aee3561551af2c: the canary fixture now covers log, backup, diagnostic and corruption-report, the four surfaces that carry content by accident rather than by design and the four the acceptance named. Repairing it found four pre-existing negative cases naming a forbidden class in snake_case where the allowlist declares kebab-case, so they resolved to nothing; a fifth naming otel-identity-attributes, which was declared nowhere; and two cases sharing one canary token, which defeats attribution. All four units serving SR-008 have landed.

findings.title: Universal adapter certification and deterministic accounting
closure_evidence: PF-015 at da930f9c961ef9d029b68e9bb1aee3561551af2c: the compatibility tuple's canonical digest is proved rather than asserted. The schema stated that the digest is over the RFC 8949 core deterministic CBOR encoding so two implementations cannot disagree about a tuple's identity, and nothing tested it; the unit's own note recorded the digest half as not landed. Two serialisations in opposite key order at every level now produce one digest, and each of the five independent dimensions changes it. Certification lifecycle and accounting reconciliation remain open under PF-016 and PF-018.

PF-018 at bc5880ae0b3d775ee9ab45d0d46ff401ac6640be: reconciliation and bounds are specified and exhaustively ordered. The acceptance allowed the author to choose two array orderings, which a first-wins reconciler satisfies on any agreeing pair; every permutation is exhausted now under a declared cap that fails rather than sampling. accounting-profile.schema.json spelled the fourth count authority reconstructed while nine artifacts spelled it exact-reconstruction, so a validator comparing them would have reported a contradiction that does not exist for every reconstruction profile, and did not fire only because the one binding it runs over is provider-reported. Summation across readings and selection-based contradiction resolution are forbidden, bounds reject rather than saturate, and capping is recorded forbidden because Token Burn is unnormalized. Nothing is certified: no vector names a certified tuple.

findings.title: Ranking authorization, immutable generations, periods, and corrections
closure_evidence: PF-021 at 7891df41e9fb4b27c7fae378beea67a9aed7e971 (audience half only): every operation carrying security: [] is declared in openapi-v1.yaml#x-public-operations with one of three admissible reasons, exactly one of which is global-board. The ranking-definition and audience separation in ranking-view-v1.schema.json is not done and PF-021 remains in-progress.

PF-021 at 986e90c29eba7733456e48cd95f99d88c3a32d0f: getLeaderboard held the global-board public reason while its path admitted global, friends, rivals and board, so the reason named one value of a path segment and the declaration covered all four: GET /leaderboards/friends/weekly answered an unauthenticated caller with a viewer-relative standing, and the board scope named no board. PF-052 had landed a note saying this operation gains a viewer parameter and loses its unauthenticated security, and did neither. RankEntry.evidence_class also admitted imported while the SQL column and the generation schema both refused it, making the public leaderboard schema the only artifact saying an import could be ranked.

PF-022 at 986e90c29eba7733456e48cd95f99d88c3a32d0f: the one active pointer did not exist: state was a five-value CHECK with no uniqueness, so two workers could each promote a generation and leave two rows active. The Cursor parameter asserted the server rejects a cursor it did not issue, one issued against a different snapshot and one issued to a different principal, while no record held an issuer, a snapshot or a principal. The refusal order is now a rule, because a presentation breaking two of them must be refused by the same one every time.

PF-023 at 986e90c29eba7733456e48cd95f99d88c3a32d0f: ranking_corrections named no participant and no period, so every row said some total somewhere moved by some amount and no rebuild could reproduce anybody's figure, while the storage contract documented an index as serving correction application across views. periods had no lifecycle at all against seasons' five checked timestamps, so a correction to a closed period was indistinguishable from a claim landing in an open one. The transition into corrected is now a moderator act under recent authentication rather than a scheduled job's.

findings.title: Social relationships, boards, presence, and notifications
closure_evidence: PF-024 at f7db7bb052cf8fef10f72ff8cbae802d13d1cf51 (social relationships only): blocked is removed from the friendship and rivalry machines and from friend_requests.state and rival_edges.state, so a directional block no longer drives a symmetric aggregate to a terminal state. Six executable cases in conformance/social/block-independence-vectors.json. Boards, presence and notifications are untouched and remain open under PF-025, PF-026 and PF-027.

findings.title: Idempotency and ambiguous commit recovery
closure_evidence: PF-019 at bf1a128ace7a3d6e8cccc2585270382da242aaee: idempotency_records keys on exactly the key_scope openapi-v1.yaml#x-idempotency-contract declares, so operation_id is inside the key and one key across two operations can no longer be answered with the other operation's recorded response. replayable-failure and abandoned replace a single failed state, which is the distinction a retry needs.

PF-020 at 868e4f867c65442faf51deb79f3a93738258de66: expiry was implemented as deletion, and a deleted key is a fresh key. idempotency_records had one lifetime column, so the only way to stop replaying past the window the wire contract declares was to delete the row — after which the next request carrying that key executed as a new mutation, which is the exact case the unit's prose said must be refused. retain_until now bounds retention separately from replay. sql-race-plans-v1.json asserted nothing: all fourteen cases carried the same four interleaving steps and one sentence, and the validator checked only ids, table existence and a flag, all of which pass on placeholders. Nineteen cases now name the rows a correct implementation leaves behind, present and absent, with 92 column assertions resolving against the DDL. Three stale justifications claiming this finding stays open for defects PF-019 and PF-049 had already repaired were struck.

findings.title: Export, deletion, retention, and backup tombstones
Release authorization, compatibility, migration, and rollback
Current-authorization recheck at every display and delivery boundary
closure_evidence: PF-021 at 7891df41e9fb4b27c7fae378beea67a9aed7e971: getPublicProfile required no viewer while projection-authorization-v1.json made directional-block deny-hard, so a blocked person could read the profile by logging out. It now requires a session and returns 401 without one. The recheck at every other display and delivery boundary is not done.

restatement.previous_form: Privacy-safe projection and current authorization, stated as a repairable cluster with no artifact set of its own.
restatement.rationale: Independent review found no independent artifact set: the aggregates named in the original wording are already owned by SR-010, SR-011 and SR-013, so the finding could not be closed by repairing anything it exclusively owned. It is restated as the invariant it actually asserts - every display and delivery boundary rechecks current authorization instead of replaying a historical snapshot - and bound to the boundary operations where that recheck is absent today. The artifact set intentionally intersects SR-010, SR-011 and SR-013 at different sites: those findings own their aggregates, this one owns the boundary. Closure is one enumerated boundary matrix plus a current-authorization check at every listed boundary, and is not satisfied by repairing any single aggregate.

findings.title: Review-record integrity: reviewed head, evidence class, and named owners

restatement.previous_form: Review, conformance, and launch-evidence integrity, owned by the document that states the finding.
restatement.rationale: The finding was self-owned: its normative owners were the semantic-review document that states it and the schema inventory, so its closure evidence would have been the same prose that defines it and no external record could contradict it. Ownership moves to the two machine records that own reviewed-head and evidence-class facts, and the prose review documents become conflicting artifacts. The disagreement is now machine-checkable: REPAIR_HEAD_REVIEW.md pins e1320a6, the semantic review states base 41ecb77, and review-target-v1.json is not-pinned with a null commit; separately the state-machine registry names persistence owners for 19 of its 26 machines that packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql does not define. Closure is a pinned review-target-v1.json whose commit exists and whose verdict is recorded, prose head claims equal to it, suite names that match what each suite executes, and one resolved persistence owner for every registered machine.

findings.title: Source-bound evidence and verifier appraisal authority
closure_evidence: PF-017 at bc5880ae0b3d775ee9ab45d0d46ff401ac6640be: source observation and normalized event now carry required operation, observer and reading identity, and the outcome vocabularies cross-resolve. They did not: observation declared aborted-unknown and unknown, the event declared aborted-known and quarantined-unknown, and no mapping existed, so an adapter observing an aborted run with an unknown remainder had to write aborted-known — recording an unknown as known. acp was missing from the observation schema's execution_mode while five other artifacts carried it, making an ACP observation unrepresentable in the schema every ACP adapter writes. TOKEN_ACCOUNTING_SPEC.md was a second vocabulary of eighteen field names existing in no schema. The OTel derivation table now states that the counter names no execution rather than implying it does.

restatement.previous_form: Stated as a contradiction whose closure required four unwritten schemas, with an artifact set that named nothing existing.
restatement.rationale: Independent review found that authoring an absent schema is a design task rather than a disagreement between two authorities, so the finding as written could not be falsified. It is split into the two things it actually contains. The contradiction part is live and now cited: one appraisal aggregate is described three ways - vibeproof-claim-v1.cddl verifier-appraisal-v1 carries seven classification dimensions, evidence-profile-policy-v1.json enumerates the same seven dimensions as server-verifier authority, and planning-schema.sql verifier_appraisals persists only provenance, continuity and integrity state with no claim digest, evidence digest, validity interval or supersession. The design part is the four artifacts already recorded planned-missing in SCHEMA_AND_INTERFACE_INVENTORY.md; they move to planned_artifacts, because a path that does not exist cannot be cited as a conflicting artifact. Closure requires both halves: the three existing authorities agree on one appraisal record, and the four planned artifacts exist and bind the exact claim, evidence, policy and result under D-077.
